discovery: The theory of cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmic structure
motivation: Guth proposed that an early epoch of exponential expansion explains the flatness, horizon and monopole problems of the hot Big Bang. Linde developed new and chaotic inflation, which made the idea a workable and predictive framework. Mukhanov, with Chibisov, showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed all cosmic structure. This yields a nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian spectrum with a small red tilt. COBE, WMAP and Planck have since confirmed these predictions with striking precision, including a spectral index of about 0.965 and acoustic peaks consistent with superhorizon adiabatic modes. Inflation ties quantum field theory and gravity directly to the observed sky. It is the first framework in which quantum fluctuations account for the large-scale universe. It has shaped four decades of cosmology and quantum-gravity research, and the coming B-mode searches remain organised around its predictions.
